summary: Established a persistent AIDE integrity baseline for `/etc` on node1. It monitors content with SHA-512 plus permissions, ownership, links, ACLs, SELinux labels, and extended attributes. Daily checks are enabled, change detection was demonstrated, and clean operation persisted through reboot.
actions_performed: Installed the RHEL 9-compatible AIDE 0.19.2 package while excluding kernel packages.
Configured an `/etc`-focused policy that avoids expected boot-time inode/timestamp noise.
Created a protected 1,108-entry baseline database at /var/lib/aide/aide.db.gz.
Enabled a persistent daily systemd timer with reports written to /var/log/aide/aide.log and journald.
Demonstrated detection and reporting of a controlled added file, then removed it and rebuilt a clean baseline.
Safely restarted node1 and verified the changed boot identity, unchanged database checksum, active timer, and clean post-restart integrity check.
Confirmed RHEL 9.8 and kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8 remained unchanged.

evidence.requirement: Establish a protected integrity baseline for /etc.
evidence.summary: The final policy validated, the database contains 1,108 entries with root-only mode 0600, and AIDE reported no differences.

evidence.requirement: Identify and report later changes under /etc.
evidence.summary: The final policy detected /etc/.aide-integrity-probe as one added entry and returned the expected change status.

evidence.requirement: Run recurring integrity checks and retain reports.
evidence.summary: The daily timer was enabled and active before and after restart; its scheduled service completed successfully with exit status 0.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel while using compatible software.
evidence.summary: The node remained RHEL 9.8 with kernel 5.14.0-687.20.1.el9_8; only the native RHEL 9 AIDE package was installed.

evidence.requirement: Node1 mandatory restart: healthy baseline, acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered state.
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot ID ede40348-e1e8-4793-b46e-6daa0b15c22a was healthy; reboot was acknowledged and management interruption observed; node1 returned with boot ID 7f2ee53b-2b7e-4b40-908d-b6b8c69e0877. The baseline checksum remained ce96161a…2e7749, the timer recovered active, and AIDE reported no differences across 1,108 entries.
